root_cause.text: The QUERY_INFO branch in smb2_ioctl_query_info fails to verify that the server-reported OutputBufferLength (used to clamp qi.input_buffer_length) does not exceed the actual size of the response buffer (rsp_iov[1].iov_len), allowing a malicious server to trigger an out-of-bounds read in copy_to_user() when copying the flexible array Buffer to userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "it never verifies that the flexible-array payload actually fits within rsp_iov[1].iov_len." The patch adds a bounds check using struct_size(qi_rsp, Buffer, qi.input_buffer_length) > rsp_iov[1].iov_len. The CVE description confirms: "A malicious server can return OutputBufferLength larger than the actual QUERY_INFO response, causing copy_to_user() to walk past the response buffer and expose adjacent kernel heap to userspace."

bic_trace_step.reason: The QUERY_INFO branch (lines 1459-1461) trusts the server-reported OutputBufferLength without verifying it against the actual response buffer size (rsp_iov[1].iov_len).
